subtopic: Types of Discontinuity
stem:
Show that the function
\(f(x) = \dfrac{5^{\cos x} - e^{\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - x\right)}}{\cot x}\), for \(x \ne \dfrac{\pi}{2}\)
\(= \log 5 - e\), for \(x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\)
has a removable discontinuity at \(x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\). Redefine the function so that it becomes continuous at \(x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\).
solution:
\(f(\pi/2) = \log 5 - e\)
Now, \(\lim_{x \to \frac{\pi}{2}} f(x) = \lim_{x \to \frac{\pi}{2}} \left( \dfrac{5^{\cos x} - e^{\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - x\right)}}{\cot x} \right)\)
Let \(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - x = t\), \(x = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - t\) as \(x \to \dfrac{\pi}{2}\), \(t \to 0\)
\(\lim_{x \to \frac{\pi}{2}} f(x) = \lim_{t \to 0} \left( \dfrac{5^{\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - t\right)} - e^{t}}{\cot\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - t\right)} \right)\)
\(= \lim_{t \to 0} \left( \dfrac{5^{\sin t} - e^{t}}{\tan t} \right)\)
\(= \lim_{t \to 0} \left( \dfrac{5^{\sin t} - 1 - e^{t} + 1}{\tan t} \right)\)
\(= \lim_{t \to 0} \left( \dfrac{(5^{\sin t} - 1) - (e^{t} - 1)}{\tan t} \right)\)
\(= \lim_{t \to 0} \left( \dfrac{\dfrac{5^{\sin t} - 1}{t} - \dfrac{e^{t} - 1}{t}}{\dfrac{\tan t}{t}} \right)\)   [As \(t \to 0\), \(t \ne 0\)]
\(= \lim_{t \to 0} \left( \dfrac{\dfrac{\sin t}{t} \times \dfrac{5^{\sin t} - 1}{\sin t} - \dfrac{e^{t} - 1}{t}}{\dfrac{\tan t}{t}} \right)\)   [\(\sin t \ne 0\)]
\(= \dfrac{(1).(\log 5) - 1}{1}\)
\(\left[ \lim_{\theta \to 0} \left( \dfrac{\sin \theta}{\theta} \right) = 1 = \lim_{\theta \to 0} \left( \dfrac{\tan \theta}{\theta} \right),\ \lim_{x \to 0} \left( \dfrac{e^{x} - 1}{x} \right) = 1,\ \lim_{x \to 0} \left( \dfrac{a^{x} - 1}{x} \right) = \log a \right]\)
\(\lim_{x \to \frac{\pi}{2}} f(x) = \log 5 - 1\)
\(f(\pi/2)\) is defined and \(\lim_{x \to \frac{\pi}{2}} f(x)\) exists
But \(\lim_{x \to \frac{\pi}{2}} f(x) \ne f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\)
\(\therefore\) the function \(f(x)\) has removable discontinuity. This discontinuity can be removed by redefining \(f(\pi/2) = \log 5 - 1\).
So the function can be redefined as follows
\(f(x) = \left( \dfrac{5^{\cos x} - e^{\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - x\right)}}{\cot x} \right)\), for \(x \ne \dfrac{\pi}{2}\)
\(= \log 5 - 1\), for \(x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\)

subtopic: Continuity of a Function at a Point
stem: If \(f(x) = \left( \dfrac{3x + 2}{2 - 5x} \right)^{\frac{1}{x}}\), for \(x \ne 0\), is continuous at \(x = 0\) then find \(f(0)\).
solution:
Given that \(f(x)\) is continuous at \(x = 0\)
\(\therefore f(0) = \lim_{x \to 0} \left( \dfrac{3x + 2}{2 - 5x} \right)^{\frac{1}{x}}\)
\(= \lim_{x \to 0} \left( \dfrac{2\left(1 + \dfrac{3x}{2}\right)}{2\left(1 - \dfrac{5x}{2}\right)} \right)^{\frac{1}{x}}\)
\(= \lim_{x \to 0} \left( \dfrac{\left(1 + \dfrac{3x}{2}\right)^{\frac{1}{x}}}{\left(1 - \dfrac{5x}{2}\right)^{\frac{1}{x}}} \right)\)
\(= \dfrac{\left[ \lim_{x \to 0} \left(1 + \dfrac{3x}{2}\right)^{\frac{2}{3x}} \right]^{\frac{3}{2}}}{\left[ \lim_{x \to 0} \left(1 - \dfrac{5x}{2}\right)^{\frac{-2}{5x}} \right]^{\frac{-5}{2}}}\)
\(= \dfrac{e^{\frac{3}{2}}}{e^{\frac{-5}{2}}}\)   \(\left[ \lim_{x \to 0} (1 + kx)^{\frac{1}{kx}} = e \right]\)
\(f(0) = e^{4}\)

subtopic: Continuity of a Function at a Point
stem:
If \(f(x)\) is defined on \(R\), discuss the continuity of \(f\) at \(x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\), where
\(f(x) = \dfrac{5^{\cos x} + 5^{-\cos x} - 2}{(3\cot x).\log\left(\dfrac{2 + \pi - 2x}{2}\right)}\), for \(x \ne \dfrac{\pi}{2}\)
\(= \dfrac{2\log 5}{3}\), for \(x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\).
solution:
Given that, for \(x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\), \(f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = \dfrac{2\log 5}{3}\),
\(\lim_{x \to \frac{\pi}{2}} f(x) = \lim_{x \to \frac{\pi}{2}} \left[ \dfrac{5^{\cos x} + 5^{-\cos x} - 2}{3(\cot x)\log\left(\dfrac{2 + \pi - 2x}{2}\right)} \right]\)
\(= \lim_{x \to \frac{\pi}{2}} \left[ \dfrac{5^{\cos x} + 5^{-\cos x} - 2}{3(\cot x)\log\left(1 + \dfrac{\pi - 2x}{2}\right)} \right]\)
Let \(\dfrac{\pi - 2x}{2} = t \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - t\) as \(x \to \dfrac{\pi}{2}\), \(t \to 0\)
\(\therefore \lim_{x \to \frac{\pi}{2}} f(x)\)
\(= \lim_{t \to 0} \left( \dfrac{5^{\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - t\right)} + 5^{-\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - t\right)} - 2}{3\cot\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - t\right).\log(1 + t)} \right)\)
\(= \lim_{t \to 0} \left( \dfrac{5^{\sin t} + 5^{-\sin t} - 2}{3(\tan t).\log(1 + t)} \right)\)
\(= \lim_{t \to 0} \left( \dfrac{5^{\sin t}\left(5^{\sin t} + 5^{-\sin t} - 2\right)}{3(\tan t)\log(1 + t).5^{\sin t}} \right)\) .........[Multiply and divide by \(5^{\sin t}\)]
\(= \lim_{t \to 0} \left( \dfrac{(5^{\sin t})^{2} + 1 - 2 \times 5^{\sin t}}{3(\tan t)\log(1 + t)(5^{\sin t})} \right)\)
\(= \lim_{t \to 0} \left( \dfrac{(5^{\sin t} - 1)^{2}}{3(\tan t).\log(1 + t).(5^{\sin t})} \right)\)
\(= \lim_{t \to 0} \left[ \dfrac{\dfrac{(5^{\sin t} - 1)^{2}}{\sin^{2} t} \times \sin^{2} t}{3(\tan t).\log(1 + t).(5^{\sin t})} \right]\)
\(t\) is small but \(t \ne 0\). Hence \(\sin t \ne 0\)
So we can multiply and divide the numerator by \(\sin^{2} t\)
\(= \lim_{t \to 0} \left( \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{5^{\sin t} - 1}{\sin t}\right)^{2} \times \left(\dfrac{\sin t}{t}\right)^{2}}{3\left(\dfrac{\tan t}{t}\right).\dfrac{\log(1 + t)}{t}.5^{\sin t}} \right)\)
[Dividing Numerator and Denominator by \(t^{2}\) as \(t \ne 0\)]
\(= \dfrac{\left[\lim_{t \to 0}\left(\dfrac{5^{\sin t} - 1}{\sin t}\right)\right]^{2} \times \lim_{t \to 0}\left(\dfrac{\sin t}{t}\right)^{2}}{3\lim_{t \to 0}\left(\dfrac{\tan t}{t}\right).\lim_{t \to 0}\left(\dfrac{\log(1 + t)}{t}\right)} \times \lim_{t \to 0}\left(\dfrac{1}{5^{\sin t}}\right)\)
\(= \dfrac{(\log 5)^{2} \times (1)}{3(1)(1)} \times \dfrac{1}{5^{0}}\)
\(\left[ \lim_{\theta \to 0}\left(\dfrac{\sin \theta}{\theta}\right) = 1,\ \lim_{\theta \to 0}\left(\dfrac{\tan \theta}{\theta}\right) = 1,\ \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{\log(1 + x)}{x}\right) = 1,\ \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{a^{x} - 1}{x}\right) = \log a \right]\)
\(\therefore \lim_{x \to \frac{\pi}{2}} f(x) = \dfrac{(\log 5)^{2}}{3}\)
\(\therefore \lim_{x \to \frac{\pi}{2}} f(x) \ne f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\)
\(\therefore f(x)\) is discontinuous at \(x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\)

subtopic: Continuity of a Function at a Point
stem:
Activity : Let \(f(x) = ax + b\) (where \(a\) and \(b\) are unknown)
\(= x^{2} + 5\) for \(x \in R\)
Find the values of \(a\) and \(b\), so that \(f(x)\) is continuous at \(x = 1\). (Fig. 8.11)
Fig. 8.11 shows the graph of \(f(x) = x^{2} + 5\) drawn only for \(x \ge 1\), with a solid dot at \((1, 6)\) and a dashed vertical segment at \(x = 1\) running from the X-axis up to that dot; no branch is drawn for \(x < 1\).
diagramNote: Fig. 8.11 — Y-axis marked 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12; X-axis marked -1, 0, 1, 2. The curve labelled f(x) = x^2 + 5 starts at the solid point (1, 6) and rises to about 12 near x = 2.5. A dashed vertical line at x = 1 joins the X-axis to (1, 6). Nothing is plotted to the left of x = 1.
_note: PRINTED AS SHOWN - possible book defect, transcribed faithfully. The stem gives no interval for either branch: it reads 'f(x) = ax + b (where a and b are unknown)' and then '= x^2 + 5 for x in R', so as printed the two branches would both apply on all of R. Fig. 8.11 draws x^2 + 5 only for x >= 1 (solid dot at (1,6)), so the intended reading is f(x) = ax + b for x < 1 and f(x) = x^2 + 5 for x >= 1. Even under that reading, continuity at x = 1 yields only a + b = 6 - one equation in two unknowns - so 'find the values of a and b' has no unique answer. The book prints no answer for Q17.
solution: [Textbook defect: the stem gives NO interval for either branch — it reads "Let \(f(x) = ax + b\) (where a and b are unknown) \(= x^2 + 5\) for \(x \in R\)" — so as printed both branches apply on all of \(R\). Fig. 8.11 settles the intent: the parabola is drawn only for \(x \ge 1\), with a solid dot at \((1, 6)\) and a dashed vertical at \(x = 1\), nothing to its left, so the linear branch is meant for \(x < 1\). Even then the question is UNDER-DETERMINED: continuity at \(x = 1\) gives only \(a + b = 6\), one equation in two unknowns. The book prints no answer for it.]

subtopic: Continuity Over an Interval
stem:
Activity : Suppose \(f(x) = px + 3\) for \(a \le x \le b\)
\(= 5x^{2} - q\) for \(b < x \le c\)
Find the condition on \(p\), \(q\), so that \(f(x)\) is continuous on \([a, c]\), by filling in the boxes.
\(f(b) = \square\)
\(\lim_{x \to b^{+}} f(x) = \square\)
\(\therefore pb + 3 = \square - q\)
\(\therefore p = \dfrac{\square}{b}\) is the required condition.
_note: Tagged '[Activity]' in the book but it is a NUMBERED exercise question with a determinate answer (continuity at x = b forces pb + 3 = 5b^2 - q, i.e. p = (5b^2 - q - 3)/b), so it is ingested on the shipped Ex 5.2 Q9 precedent rather than skipped as an Activity box. The empty boxes the book prints are rendered as \square. The book prints no answer for Q18.
